text.p: Mobil Corp said Friday it received a $78.3 million judgment in its favor against the federal government in litigation concerning oil and gas leases offshore North Carolina.

This judgment, by the U.S. Court of Federal Claims in Washington, D.C., recognizes Mobil's right to rescind five Outer Continental Shelf leases and to be reimbursed for the purchase price, the company explained.
In 1992, Mobil and other lessees sued, seeking monetary damages for the government's failure to allow development of leases offshore Alaska, Florida and North Carolina.

In 1995, Mobil and the other lessees settled the Alaska/Florida portion of the litigation. Following that settlement, Mobil received $40 million on August 25, 1996, for full reimbursement of lease bonus and rentals and partial reimbursement of other direct expenses.
On March 14, 1996, the Federal Claims Court ruled in favor of Mobil and the other lessees for the North Carolina claim, granting motions for summary judgement.
Today's announcement is the result of that judgment, Mobil said, noting the government has not yet announced whether it will appeal the judgment.
